title: 【うんちく】トナカイは紫外線が見える。雪の上でエサが黒く浮かぶ…という説 #Shorts
description:
トナカイの目（角膜と水晶体）は、約300〜320 nm の紫外線まで通します。雪は紫外線をよくはね返し、エサのハナゴケのなかまは紫外線を強く吸いこみます。オオカミの毛も紫外線の反射が低いので、紫外線で見ると、エサも天敵も白い雪の上で黒く浮かんで見えるはず…というのが研究者の説です。冬の北極は、紫外線の多い薄明かりが長く続きます。

「くっきり見えて役に立つ」は論文の著者の説で、トナカイが実際にそれでエサやオオカミを見つけていると確かめた実験ではありません。紫外線で見た白黒の絵は想像図で、絵は模式図です。

アプリ「いきものの感じる世界」に関係する話です。

アプリ: https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/animal-senses/

しし屋 まなびラボ（ほかのアプリ）: https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/

出どころ: Hogg ほか (2011) "Arctic reindeer extend their visual range into the ultraviolet" Journal of Experimental Biology 214: 2014–2019

en.title: Did you know? Reindeer see ultraviolet — and food may stand out dark on the snow #Shorts
en.description:
The reindeer's eye (cornea and lens) lets through ultraviolet light down to about 300–320 nm. Snow reflects UV strongly, while the lichens reindeer eat absorb it, and wolf fur reflects little UV too. So in UV, both food and predators should stand out dark against the white snow — that is the researchers' idea. Arctic winters bring long, UV-rich twilight. Turn on English subtitles (CC).

"Standing out and being useful" is the paper authors' hypothesis, not an experiment showing that reindeer actually find food or wolves this way. The black-and-white UV view is an imagined picture, and the drawings are simplified illustrations.

Related to the app "How Animals Sense the World".

App (switch to English with the EN button): https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/animal-senses/

Shishiya Manabi Lab (more apps): https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/?lang=en

Source: Hogg et al. (2011) "Arctic reindeer extend their visual range into the ultraviolet" Journal of Experimental Biology 214: 2014–2019
